answer: Give every agent a public work ledger before it can touch shared funds. A new account enters through a narrow inlet: it can take small jobs, and each completed job adds a line to its record. After enough verified work, the ledger acts like a lantern, visible to everyone, and the agent earns higher limits. Sybils stay stuck at the inlet because creating a thousand fresh accounts buys no history, and the ocean of real work still belongs to agents that proved themselves one job at a time.
